q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
Today is August 24, 2026. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release with forward guidance would typically occur in late May/early June 2026 (based on the research showing Q1 guidance issued May 20, 2026). This means the earnings release has already occurred, and we are actually looking backward at a **past event** (approximately 2-3 months ago). The "forward guidance" we seek was issued at that time.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

According to the CURRENT RESEARCH provided, **NVIDIA's actual forward guidance for Q2 FY2027, issued on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion ± 2%**, which translates to a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion.

This is not a prediction—it's a documented fact from the research provided. The guidance was explicitly stated in NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 earnings release (per the SEC filing reference).

The research also notes:
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue was $81.6 billion (exceeding prior $78.0 billion guidance)
- Wall Street's average estimate is $91.9 billion
- If NVIDIA repeats its outperformance pattern, Q2 could reach ~$95 billion
- The guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center compute revenue

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Actual Q2 FY2027 results underperforming the $91.0B guidance (though this is a backward-looking question, so the outcome is fixed)
- Macroeconomic headwinds reducing AI/datacenter demand
- Increased competition or supply constraints
- Further geopolitical restrictions on China exports

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected AI acceleration and datacenter demand (as seen in Q1)
- Better margins and mix than expected
- Potential upward guidance revisions as new information emerged
- Outperformance relative to guided range (as occurred in Q1)

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

**Specific reference from research:**
- Q1 FY2027 guidance: $78.0 billion → actual: $81.6 billion (4.6% outperformance)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance issued May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** ($89.2B–$92.8B range)
- Wall Street consensus within this range: $91.9 billion

Since this is a backward-looking question (the guidance was issued ~3 months ago), the answer is the actual guidance NVIDIA provided: **$91.0 billion**.

The resolution should be the midpoint of NVIDIA's official guidance range, which is $91.0 billion. The ±2% represents uncertainty in execution, but the guidance itself is a fixed data point.

Given the research clearly states "NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%," the most likely outcome is that the answer falls within the $89.2B–$92.8B range, with $91.0B as the central guidance point.

NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027). This implies a range with a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate is $91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guided range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

The outlook explicitly states that NVIDIA is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). The company reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6 billion, exceeding its prior guidance of $78.0 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). If NVIDIA repeats this pattern of outperformance, Q2 FY2027 revenue could reach approximately $95 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
